summary: A dense engine-building euro where you move a pawn along a shared track to trigger actions, research theories, and build tools, converting resources into an ever-improving personal engine. It plays like a tighter, more mathematical cousin of Tzolk'in, rewarding players who can plan several turns of resource conversion ahead.
praised: high replayability from variable setup and asymmetric research paths
criticised: dry, sterile theme that barely surfaces during play
significant analysis paralysis from the branching decision space
can feel overly mathematical/optimization-puzzle-like rather than exciting

interaction.kind: drafting limited research tiles and action spaces on a shared board
interaction.detail: Players mostly build their own tech track and toolbox, but the open draft of tiles/cards and the shared map of universities/cities means a tile or spot you want can be taken first. Most of the state (your track, tools, card engine) is private; the shared parts are the drafting pool and a handful of contested locations.

scoring.how_you_win: You win by accumulating the most VP from advancing your four tech tracks and playing/fulfilling Discovery cards, tallied once the game's end trigger closes out the final round.
